title.narrative: Multisectoral (WASH, CCCM, ESNFIs, Protection, MPC) emergency support to relocated IDPs and host communities in Central Zone, Tigray Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe most vulnerable Ethiopians are still facing significant levels of humanitarian need in 2023 as a result of several, frequently overlapping disasters. The Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA), which was signed in November 2022, has made possible to scale up aid in Northern Ethiopia including the restoration of public services. In Tigray, more than 70% of IDP sites, according to data from the Clusters, are schools, and more than 200,000 IDPs live in 109 schools. Due the need to resume activities in the schools, this project aims to give support to relocated IDPs and restore public services through rehabilitation and maintenance of schools in Adwa, Central Zone of Tigray. The project will be carried out through a consortium composed by COOPI, OSSDH and NEXUS Ethiopia which will allow to have an area-based approach and integrated intervention to ensure a safe relocation of IDPs as well as the restoration of the educational activities through a multi-sectoral approach that will cover WASH, protection, Shelter NFI and cash needs of IDPs and educational communities in 3 targeted schools of Adwa. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtSpecifically, COOPI will cover water supply, sanitation, hygiene as well as the Multi-purpose cash assistance, while NEXUS Ethiopia will implement activities under the sector of ES/NFI, and OSSDH will cover the protection needs and will ensure the Area-Based Approach through the sector of CCCM. lt/pgtltpgtUnder the sector of WASH, the project will benefit 3390 among students, schools staff and IDPs. At the same time, COOPI will work on MPC reaching 2000 beneficiaries. Additionally, the project will target IDPs that will be relocated through Shelter support and will reach 4,220 beneficiaries. Furthermore, under the protection sector OSSDH will reach 6,082 IDPs through case management, psychosocial support as well as raising awareness campaigns. Finally, OSSDH through the CCCM sector will support the voluntary relocation and the creation of ABA in IDPs sites in Adwa, these activity will reach the needs of 5714 IDPs as well as 3 targeted schools and their basin of users. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtRevision:lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtFollowing an assessment conducted by Nexus Ethiopia between the 5th and 10th of February on the rental market in Adwa and collecting intentions from the beneficiaries, it appeared that the cash for rent would not be viable in Adwa town. ltbrgtIt also appeared that the alternative site to build the 28 duplex shelters (Adwa Industrial Site) was no longer viable. ltbrgtA field visit mission was conducted by COOPI from March 19th to March 21st which led to the organization of an Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) workshop including the IDPs, the local authorities, the relevant cluster representatives and the consortium members. ltbrgt1. COOPI and partners propose to extend support to Negeste Saba Primary School. NS Primary was previously occupied by IDPs but is presently unoccupied. At the new school, COOPI and partners propose to build 12-15 Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS) and rehabilitate the premises and WASH facilities.ltbrgt2. NS Prep will be freed of IDPs and rehabilitated, and NS Secondary would become an IDP site. This would make 15 classrooms available for rehabilitation. COOPI and partners propose to build 22 Duplex shelters on secondary side, rehabilitate the Preparatory side premises and rehabilitate/construct WASH facilities on both the secondary and preparatory side. To isolate both compounds, COOPI and partners will build a fence.ltbrgt3. With the Tsion/Dr. Tsegay complex being totally occupied by IDPs, the site will remain an IDP site. COOPI and partners, therefore, propose to build 15 Duplex shelters and construct/rehabilitate WASH facilities for the IDPs.ltbrgt4. At Korea School, COOPI and partners propose to construct 6-9 TLS and rehabilitate the premises and WASH facilities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
